objective: Settle the factual open points of the 0.3.0 pi integration plan about pi itself, from pi's current official sources.
scope: Context: /home/user/holyagent/docs/pi/ (README.md, extensions.md, providers.md, orchestration.md, claude-parity.md, auto-mode.md, installation.md) records research against pi 1.4.0 (earendil-works/pi, packages @earendil-works/pi-*). The open points list: /home/user/holyagent-work/pi-open.md.

Answer, each with a dated source link: (1.1) pi's current stable version and release cadence, and whether docs/pi's 1.4.0 facts still hold for it (list what changed for extensions, packages, providers, RPC/JSON modes and codemode); (6.21) an existing maintained pi extension or MCP server that gives web search and fetch; (6.22) an existing pi extension or tool that can watch a long-running command such as 'gh pr checks --watch' without blocking (a monitor or background-process tool); (6.23, 6.24) how a pi package can load or depend on pi's example extensions (todo.ts, question.ts, questionnaire.ts) and whether maintained published packages already provide a todo list and an ask/question tool; (7.25) what pi's docs recommend for driving child pi processes (rpc vs json with -p) and any maintained subagent or orchestration extension; (7.27) PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS default and whether it can be raised; (7.28) the documented effect of PI_OFFLINE, PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK and PI_TELEMETRY; (8.31) whether the openai-codex provider uses a documented endpoint; (9.36) whether Bun is a documented or working way to run pi.
Use pi.dev, the earendil-works/pi repository and its docs, and npm. Separate sourced facts from inference.
constraints: Read-only: write no files and make no git writes; the full answer goes in the report.
Keep working until done; stop and report. Report in under 600 words, one short entry per open point id with its answer, source link and date, and 'unknown' where the sources do not say.

criteria.text: Each open point gets a sourced answer or an explicit unknown

result:
result: All points answered below. Pi is now 1.5.0, and the 1.4.0 facts in docs/pi mostly hold. Nothing in the sources contradicts them.

**1.1 Version and cadence.** Stable is 1.5.0, published 2 Nov 2026 (npm, GitHub releases). 1.4.0 was dated 21 Oct 2026 (codeagentswarm guide, a third-party source), so that gap was about 12 days. Between 7 May and 22 Jun 2026 npm shows about 19 releases from 0.74.0 to 0.79.10, so "weekly" holds only loosely.
- Changes in 1.5.0 per the release notes:
  - Extensions: tool-argument validation now runs on `@earendil-works/pi-schema` (breaking). TypeBox-only features (`Type.Refine`, `BigInt`, codecs) no longer apply. `Type`, `Static` and `TSchema` imports still work. `pi.exec` gained `maxBuffer` and `truncated`. Extension packages can show a changelog after an update.
  - Packages: added `pi.changelogPath`. The package docs say host-provided packages (`pi-ai`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-coding-agent`, `pi-tui`, `typebox`) go in `peerDependencies` with a `"*"` range, not in `dependencies`.
  - Providers: new GPT-6.1 Terra, default OpenAI model is now `gpt-6.1-sol`, and the model catalog moved to models.dev v2. The Kimi provider ids are unchanged, but their default model changed in some release after 1.4.0 (moonshotai and the others now default to Kimi K2.7 Code). I did not read the Kimi docs for 5.15.
  - RPC and JSON: no change listed.
  - Codemode: no change listed. `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` default is still 2.
  - Other: `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` added, and MCP OAuth defaults changed.
- Sources: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases (2 Nov 2026), https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. Release dates before 1.4.0 are only partly shown.

**6.21 Web search and fetch.** Maintained candidates:
- `pi-web-access` (`web_search`, `fetch_content`).
- `pi-web-kit` (`web_search`, `web_fetch`, with Exa among its providers; its `web_search` requires a `purpose` parameter for Exa).
- `@zhcsyncer/pi-search-hub`.
- Pi itself has built-in MCP (the 1.5.0 `pi-mcp` dependency), so an MCP server also works.
- Sources: https://pi.dev/packages/pi-web-access, https://pi.dev/packages/pi-web-kit. Pages undated, scraped 7 Nov 2026. Maintenance status is unverified beyond the listings.

**6.22 Watching a long command.**
- `@aliou/pi-processes` runs a command in the background and wakes the model when output matches a readiness or error marker, or when the process exits. It names `pi-event-monitor` and `pi-monitor-plugin` as related packages.
- `pi-background-tasks` offers `/bg` with durable completion notifications.
- Inference: either could run `gh pr checks --watch`. I did not test that.
- Sources: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aliou/pi-processes, https://pi.dev/packages/pi-background-tasks.
- Pi core ships no background bash; pi.dev says "use tmux".

**6.23 and 6.24 Example extensions and todo/ask packages.**
- The docs say nothing about loading examples from a package. A package may depend on other Pi packages if the tarball includes them, and references them through their `node_modules` resource paths (packages.md, 1.5.0). Whether the Pi tarball's `examples/` can be referenced this way is unknown.
- Maintained published packages exist for the same jobs:
  - Todo: `@juicesharp/rpiv-todo` (97K downloads/month), `@zhcsyncer/pi-todo`.
  - Ask: `@juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question` (169K/month), `@zhcsyncer/pi-ask-user-question`.
- Source: https://pi.dev/packages, 7 Nov 2026.
- Whether an example can be reused unchanged: unknown.

**7.25 Driving child pi processes.**
- Docs describe `--mode json` as one invocation that streams events and exits. `--mode rpc` is a long-lived JSONL protocol on stdin/stdout. The docs also say to use the SDK for in-process hosts and the exported `RpcClient` for subprocess TypeScript clients.
- No recommendation between rpc and json is given for children.
- Maintained subagent extensions:
  - `pi-subagents` (nicobailon, 0.87.0, 7 Nov 2026, about 207K downloads/week, needs Pi 1.2.0 or newer).
  - `@tintinweb/pi-subagents` (0.23.1, 4 Nov 2026).
- Sources: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/rpc.md, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/json.md, https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-subagents.

**7.27 `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS`.**
- Default is 2. It counts workers alive across all sessions in the process, each script may use up to 256 MB, and the docs say to raise it for in-process subagents.
- Scripts wait up to 60 seconds for a free worker (changelog); the env table says only that they wait.
- I did not read anything on `parentToolCallId` restrictions beyond the changelog line about nested calls emitting events with it.
- Source: https://pi.dev/docs/latest/environment-variables, matching the 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 docs.

**7.28 `PI_OFFLINE`, `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`, `PI_TELEMETRY`.**
- 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 docs: `PI_OFFLINE` "disable automatic network activity, including model catalog refreshes". `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK` disables the pi.dev latest-version request. `PI_TELEMETRY=0` overrides install/update telemetry and provider attribution headers.
- The 0.82/0.84 docs worded `PI_OFFLINE` as covering update checks, package updates and install ping (settings.md v0.84.2); I did not confirm that the 1.5.0 wording still covers them. For certainty, set all three.
- `--offline` is equivalent to `PI_OFFLINE=1`.
- Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/environment-variables.md.

**8.31 `openai-codex` endpoint.**
- The provider source at v1.4.0 uses base URL `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api`, authenticates with the ChatGPT Plus/Pro OAuth login, and was named "OpenAI Codex (legacy)". The default endpoint is `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` per the pi-fast docs, which are third party.
- The changelog shows the "(legacy)" label was reverted, so it is shown as "OpenAI Codex" again. A "Sign in with ChatGPT" login on the `openai` provider also exists.
- I found no official doc describing the chatgpt.com backend as a public API. It is a code-only endpoint. Whether that fits the no-undocumented-endpoints rule is the root's decision.
- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/v1.4.0/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex.ts.

**9.36 Bun.**
- pi.dev lists `bun add -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` as an install command.
- Runtime is Node: the `cli.js` shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env node`. In issue #6237 (6 Jul 2026) the maintainer said "we can't have a shebang that works for all runtimes". A user in that issue could run it with `bun <path>/cli.js`.
- A third-party post (29 Oct 2026) says the package also ships `dist/bun/cli.js`, and the repo's own `scripts/build-binaries.sh` compiles that file into standalone binaries with `bun build --compile`.
- Pi's `npmCommand` setting accepts `["bun"]` for package installs (issue #4160). No official doc says Bun is a supported way to run Pi.

blockers: none
questions: none
notes: Several package pages are undated, so their maintenance status is thin evidence. I did not fetch Kimi, Windows, or the `examples/` tarball contents.

evidence:
Each open point gets a sourced answer or an explicit unknown: 1.1, 6.21, 6.22, 6.23, 6.24, 7.25, 7.27, 7.28, 8.31 and 9.36 are answered above with links and dates. The unknowns are marked: example reuse (6.24), whether the 1.5.0 `PI_OFFLINE` text covers the update check and install ping (7.28), and the `parentToolCallId` restriction (7.27).
